topic: Selective / conformal prediction with cluster- or site-level (hierarchical, multi-center, hospital-level, federated) exchangeability or cluster-robust coverage guarantees
verdict: NO COLLISION FOUND. No located paper combines site-as-unit exchangeability with a finite-sample (betting / e-value) certificate on answered-set error for a selective predictor, plus label-shift correction with cluster-robust uncertainty, on multi-hospital clinical data. The lane is crowded on each component separately: (a) hierarchical / two-layer exchangeability for distribution-free prediction (Dunn-Wasserman-Ramdas; Lee-Barber-Willett; Lee-Ren e-values), (b) multi-site / federated conformal coverage incl. label shift and per-site risk control (Lu et al.; Plassier et al.; Liu et al.; Yang-Jin; Shahid 2026), (c) e-value / betting-certified selective prediction (Bai-Jin SCoRE; Zhou-Wang audit, whose grouped-deployment failure finding is essentially CertGate's motivating claim). Eleven NEAR_MISS entries a reviewer would plausibly expect to see cited; four BACKGROUND.

papers.title: Distribution-Free Prediction Sets for Two-Layer Hierarchical Models
papers.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association 118(544):2491-2502 (arXiv 1809.07441, 2018)
papers.authors: Robin Dunn, Larry Wasserman, Aaditya Ramdas
papers.why: The canonical treatment of groups (e.g., repeated observations per patient, or units within sites) as the exchangeable unit for distribution-free prediction: CDF pooling, single subsampling and repeated subsampling constructions with finite-sample coverage. It is the classic that establishes 'cluster, not record, is the exchangeable unit' for conformal-style guarantees. No selective prediction, no e-value/betting certificate on answered error, no label shift, no clinical multi-site validation. Reviewers in the conformal community will expect it in related work as the origin of hierarchical exchangeability.

papers.title: Distribution-free inference with hierarchical data
papers.authors: Yonghoon Lee, Rina Foygel Barber, Rebecca Willett
papers.why: Derives a hierarchical form of exchangeability for grouped/repeated-measurement data and extends conformal prediction and jackknife+ to it, including a 'second-moment coverage' property that controls conditional miscoverage across groups. Directly overlaps CertGate's exchangeable-sites baseline (site as the unit); differs in target (prediction sets, not answered-set error certificate), no betting/e-process, no label shift, no clinical data. Expected citation for the site-level exchangeability premise.

papers.title: Selection from Hierarchical Data with Conformal e-values
papers.why: Closest single overlap on the 'cluster-as-unit + e-values + selection with error control' axis: constructs valid conformal e-values for hierarchical (grouped) data via subsampling and hierarchical constructions, and uses e-BH to select individuals with FDR control. Differs materially: the error criterion is FDR over selected individuals via e-BH, not a finite-sample certificate that a thresholded selective classifier's answered error is <= alpha with confidence 1-delta; no test-martingale/betting construction, no label-shift mode, no clinical multi-site data. A reviewer would still expect it to be positioned against.

papers.title: Federated Conformal Predictors for Distributed Uncertainty Quantification
papers.authors: Charles Lu, Yaodong Yu, Sai Praneeth Karimireddy, Michael I. Jordan, Ramesh Raskar
papers.why: Introduces 'partial exchangeability' across clients (sites) so that conformal coverage holds when client distributions differ; evaluated on medical imaging. Overlaps the multi-site premise of CertGate but the guarantee is coverage of prediction sets under a client-mixture, not a selective-prediction error certificate; no e-values, no label-shift correction with cluster-robust budget. Standard citation for federated/multi-site conformal.

papers.title: Conformal Prediction for Federated Uncertainty Quantification Under Label Shift
papers.authors: Vincent Plassier, Mehdi Makni, Aleksandr Rubashevskii, Eric Moulines, Maxim Panov
papers.why: Federated conformal prediction where each client's label distribution differs from the population; importance weights reflecting each client's label shift are used in a federated weighted-quantile computation (DP-FedCP) with valid-coverage guarantees. This is the nearest prior on CertGate's BBSE label-shift mode in a multi-site setting. Differences: prediction sets rather than certified selective abstention; the importance weights are not budgeted with cluster-robust uncertainty into a decline branch; not clinical eICU-scale.

papers.title: Multi-Source Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
papers.authors: Yi Liu, Alexander W. Levis, Sharon-Lise Normand, Larry Han
papers.why: Distribution-free prediction intervals for a target site's unobserved outcomes, pooling multiple heterogeneous source sites and adaptively up/down-weighting sites; applied to pediatric cardiac-surgery hospital length-of-stay. Same multi-hospital problem framing (sites as heterogeneous sources under shift), but coverage is asymptotic (parametric rates via efficient influence functions), not a finite-sample site-unit certificate; no selective prediction, no e-values.

papers.title: Multi-Distribution Robust Conformal Prediction
papers.why: Finite-sample coverage that is uniformly valid across multiple source distributions (max-p aggregation), motivated in the introduction by clinical risk models trained on several hospitals where the test patient's site is unknown. Overlaps CertGate's 'guarantee that survives site heterogeneity' motive but delivers worst-case-over-sites coverage of prediction sets, not answered-set error control for a selective gate; no e-process, no label shift, no clinical validation.

papers.title: When Average Calibration Fails: Site-Conditional Federated Conformal Risk Control (v1 title: When Calibration Fails the Vulnerable Hospital: Federated Conformal Risk Control via Risk-Curve Shrinkage)
papers.why: Shows on 20-institution FeTS-2022 brain-tumor data that pooled conformal risk control protects the average hospital yet violates the risk target at 40% of sites, and proposes site-conditional finite-sample risk control via risk-curve shrinkage and equal-site weighting. This is the same 'aggregate-vs-individual site' failure signature CertGate measures (E1 dispersion diagnostic, E7 record-vs-site comparator), in the same 2026 window. Differs: segmentation risk control, no abstention/selective gate, no e-value certificate, no label shift, no pre-registered protocol. Reviewers will expect it cited or contrasted.

papers.title: A hierarchical conformal framework for uncertainty-aware length of stay prediction in multi-hospital settings (arXiv version: Adaptive Conformal Prediction via Bayesian Uncertainty Weighting for Hierarchical Healthcare Data)
papers.authors: Marzieh Amiri Shahbazi, Ali Baheri, Nasibeh Azadeh-Fard
papers.why: Hierarchical (hospital/region) healthcare data, group-aware conformal calibration on 61,538 admissions across 3,793 US hospitals, published in a Springer Nature venue adjacent to the target collection. Overlaps CertGate on the multi-hospital conformal framing but delivers marginal interval coverage for LOS regression via a hybrid Bayesian-conformal weighting; hospitals are not the unit of an independence argument, no selective prediction, no finite-sample answered-error certificate, no label shift. Same-domain expectation for citation.

papers.title: False Sense of Safety in Selective Signal Classification: Auditing Bound Tightness and Exchangeability for Risk Control
papers.why: Audits selective prediction with distribution-free risk control (with confidence 1-delta, error among accepted inputs <= alpha) using Hoeffding, Clopper-Pearson and betting (WSR) upper confidence bounds, and finds that under grouped deployment (unseen machine types / generators) certified rules overrun in 9-30% of trials because the record-level exchangeability premise breaks; a per-group threshold restores validity at severe coverage cost. That is precisely CertGate's motivating claim (record-as-unit certificate fails under cluster structure) with the same bound family, but on audio/image forensics, and it stops at diagnosis rather than proposing a site-as-unit certificate, a label-shift mode, or clinical validation.

papers.title: Conformal Selective Prediction with General Risk Control (SCoRE)
papers.why: Selective prediction with finite-sample control of a user-defined bounded risk among trusted (answered) cases, built from a class of generalized e-values under exchangeability, with a health-risk-prediction application. Overlaps CertGate's component (2) (e-value-based certificate on answered-set risk) closely; does not treat sites/clusters as the exchangeable unit, has no label-shift mode, and is not validated on multi-hospital data. A reviewer would expect it in the selective-prediction-with-e-values related work.

papers.title: Group-Weighted Conformal Prediction
papers.why: Weighted conformal prediction when the train/test likelihood ratio is piecewise constant across groups (e.g., sites), sharpening WCP by estimating group weights; relevant background for group-wise reweighting between sites but addresses covariate shift by known groups, not label shift or cluster-as-unit certification.

papers.title: Conformal causal inference for cluster randomized trials: model-robust inference without asymptotic approximations
papers.authors: Bingkai Wang, Fan Li, Mengxin Yu
papers.why: Finite-sample conformal prediction intervals for counterfactual differences at cluster and individual level in cluster-randomized trials, using clusters as the randomization/exchangeability unit; parallel 'cluster as unit' logic in a causal-inference setting, not selective prediction or risk models.

papers.title: Act or Defer: Error-Controlled Decision Policies for Medical Foundation Models (StratCP)
papers.authors: Ying Jin, Intae Moon, Marinka Zitnik
papers.why: Stratified conformal act-or-defer policy for medical foundation models: an action arm with FDR control on acted-upon patients and a deferral arm with selection-conditional coverage; finite-sample guarantees. Related clinical selective-prediction-with-error-budget framing, but strata are not sites, no cluster-level independence argument, no e-process certificate on answered error rate, imaging/pathology rather than multi-hospital tabular risk.

papers.title: Anytime-Valid Confirmation of Label-Shift Corrections
papers.why: Shows the per-observation likelihood ratio between a label-shift-corrected predictive and the source predictive is a conditional e-value, giving a test martingale (Ville) for anytime-valid confirmation of a pre-specified label-shift correction. Touches CertGate's e-value + BBSE intersection but validates a correction sequentially rather than certifying answered-set error, with no site structure or clinical data.
